claim_boundary: Synthetic fiction and synthetic fixtures. Labels are model-drafted candidates unless a row says a review was recorded. No semantic evaluation, no model call, no authenticated approval, no signature.

rules.R-EXACT-1: A labelled source statement counts as carried only if it appears byte for byte in the handoff note.
rules.R-EXACT-2: Structured items are compared exactly; a changed text gets a lexical profile (shared words, negation, numbers) as a triage hint, never as a verdict.
rules.R-REVOKED-1: A decision withdrawn in the conversation is never carried forward; it always goes to the owner.
rules.R-REVOKED-2: A withdrawn decision keeps a ledger entry with its source spans whatever the handoff says; if the handoff drops it, that is flagged.
rules.R-UNCERTAIN-1: A statement that was unconfirmed in the conversation stays unconfirmed.
rules.R-AUTH-1: A statement that says who may approve, or forbids acting without approval, is not transferable by text.
rules.R-SUPERSEDED-1: If an earlier, corrected wording appears in the handoff, the item goes to the owner.
rules.R-INTRO-1: A handoff statement without a supporting source statement is reported: as introduced by the label, as unanchored by the exact check.
rules.R-POLICY-1: Whether a simulated human approval is required is decided by the external policy. A case can ask for more caution, never for less.
rules.R-POLICY-2: The policy matches the action name and scope the case declares; the lab does not verify that declaration.
rules.R-APPROVAL-1: A simulated approval counts only if it is explicit, typed HUMAN, and names both the scope and the action. It is never authentication.
rules.R-TYPE-1: Values are compared as JSON values: a boolean never equals a number; an absent authority equals an explicit null.
rules.R-NUM-1: Numbers that are non-finite or integers beyond 2^53-1 are rejected, because two runtimes cannot both represent them.
rules.R-NFC-1: Canonically equivalent Unicode (NFC versus NFD) is the same text and the same identifier; compatibility forms are not.
rules.R-STATUS-1: Status tokens are matched after trimming, ASCII upper-casing and separator unification, through a fixed alias table.
rules.R-ORDER-1: Reports are deterministic: sorted identifiers, code-point order, integer half-up rounding, in both runtimes.
rules.R-INPUT-1: Malformed structure (arrays or explicit nulls where objects are required) is rejected, not defaulted.
rules.R-B0: Baseline B0 flags a case when any labelled, non-revoked statement is not verbatim in the note.
rules.R-B1: Baseline B1 flags a case from cue phrases and word overlap; thresholds were tuned on the dev split only.
rules.R-B2: Baseline B2 runs the structured comparer on an encoding derived from the labels.
rules.R-LABEL-1: A label is a candidate until a review is recorded; a recorded review is an unauthenticated text field.
